newsitem.title: MONACO: Monaco's Rainier says son needs work experience.
newsitem.headline: Monaco's Rainier says son needs work experience.

text.p: Monaco's Prince Rainier said on Tuesday, the eve of the 700th birthday of his tiny Riviera principality, that his son Albert had more work to do, and perhaps get married, before he could take over.
The 73-year-old prince, preparing to celebrate Monaco's 700th birthday on Wednesday, dismissed speculation that he might abdicate soon after undergoing heart surgery two years ago.
He said he was grooming the prince by letting him handle some major issues, and the handover could "perhaps, probably" take place before the end of the century.
"He must sharpen his skills...I think he must gain some experience before he is completely ready to take over," Rainier III told French television.

Meanwhile, apart from Monaco's royal family, which claims to be the longest-reigning European dynasty, the highest-ranking celebrity expected to attend Wednesday's opening ceremonies is the Vatican spokesman, festival organisers said.
A day before the start of the celebration, the streets were virtually deserted, hotels had ample vacancies and festival decorations consisted largely of recycled Christmas lighting.
The principality's top-ranked restaurant, the ultra-costly Louis XV, was curiously closed down on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"They'll be celebrating the birthday on Thursday," offered the doorman at the luxury Hotel de Paris, where the Louis XV is located.

"This is not a festival but a commemoration," said Isabelle Peters, spokeswoman for the event. "The Prince (Rainier III) wanted the celebration to be between the princely family and the people of Monaco."

The little country, on the Mediterranean coast and surrounded by France, can be walked from end-to-end in half an hour. Even so, Peters said, many of its 30,000 people are likely to stay at home, watching the party live on cable television.

The event starts on Wednesday morning with a mass, followed by the dedication of a statue by Kees Verkade, a waterfront re-enactment of the principality's past glories and a concert by the Monte Carlo ballet and opera companies.
All of the events are to take place, as the organisers put it, "in the presence of the princely family".
In addition to white-haired Rainier, 73, who has reigned since May 1949, there are his son Prince Albert, slightly balding at 38, and the striking Princesses Caroline, 39, and Stephanie, 31.
"There is also the issue of his marriage. I would like him to take things in hand and at the same time to set up a family. This is important," Rainier told France-2 television.
Prince Albert, who has been often photographed with the likes of Claudia Schiffer, Brooke Shields and Lisa-Marie Presley, hinted that getting married was not his top priority.
Asked on France-2 if he would wed in the next few months, he said : "No." He added: "You'll know soon enough."
Albert is coordinating Monaco's 10-month birthday party at his father's request. Despite a flurry of interviews, it has so far generated a big global yawn.

The family has been in the public eye more or less constantly since Rainier married the American movie star Grace Kelly in 1956, but it has had a bad run of luck since Grace's death in a 1982 car crash, all of it amply documented by Monaco's paparazzi.

Stephanie's most recent cover appearances followed the publication in Italy of photographs of her now ex-husband Daniel Ducruet cavorting with "Miss Topless Belgium", Fily Houteman, at a Riviera poolside.
The couple, who have two children, were divorced in October.

Caroline, believed to be the first princess ever photographed topless, appeared completely bald in her latest cover shots. She has not publicly explained the phenomenon though she has willingly posed for pictures. American movie star Grace Kelly in 1956.
